ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the diagram, the five circles have the same radii and touch as shown. The square joins the centres of the four outer circles. What is the ratio of the area of the shaded part of all five circles to the area of the unshaded parts of the circles?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are five circles with the same radius: one circle is in the middle and is entirely shaded gray; the other four circles are respectively located near the four corners of the square. The four vertices of the square are exactly the centers of the four outer circles. In each outer circle, the angular region that falls inside the square is shaded gray, and the remaining part is not shaded gray. Reasoning: Let the radius of each circle be r. The middle circle is all shaded gray, with area πr^2. For each outer circle, the two sides of the square form a right angle at the center of that outer circle, so the shaded part that falls inside the square is a 90° sector, that is, one fourth of the area of that circle, with area πr^2/4. The shaded area of the four outer circles totals 4 × πr^2/4 = πr^2. Therefore the total shaded area is πr^2 + πr^2 = 2πr^2. The total area of the five circles is 5πr^2, so the unshaded area is 5πr^2 − 2πr^2 = 3πr^2. Therefore the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area is 2πr^2 : 3πr^2 = 2:3.

raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, the five circles have the same radii and touch as shown. The square joins the centres of the four outer circles. What is the ratio of the area of the shaded part of all five circles to the area of the unshaded parts of the circles?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the shaded region consists of the whole middle circle plus the portions of each of the four outer circles that lie inside the square. The square’s four vertices are the centres of the four outer circles, so at each outer circle the shaded part inside the square is exactly a 90-degree sector, i.e. one quarter of that circle. From the text, all five circles have equal radius, say r. Therefore the shaded area is one full central circle plus four quarter-circles: πr^2 + 4(πr^2/4) = 2πr^2. The total area of all five circles is 5πr^2, so the unshaded area is 5πr^2 − 2πr^2 = 3πr^2. Hence the shaded-to-unshaded ratio is 2:3.
